idea: Systematic move pairs: move 1 = every sigma swap of the preimages of the demanded lines' points and every flag swap touching them or the demanded lines; move 2 = every sigma swap and near flag swap touching the failing vertices left by move 1. Early-abort batch cost (plusopt2 walk model). f5: 185,814 first moves, 11 with cost <=24 (min 6), 752,811 second moves, best pair stays 2. g61: no first move with cost <=24.
next: Pair search from the demand set is exhausted at cost 2 (f5) and stalls above 24 (g61). Next: plateau walk over cost-2 states, accepting neutral pairs with a tabu list, then the pair test at each state with move 1 = all sigma swaps plus flags touching the failing vertices.

idea: tabu search over sigma swaps: every swap (a,b) with a in up to 4 hot points and b any point; tenure 8-24 steps; restart from best after 40 stalled steps with 3 random swaps
command: SEED=7 SECS=420 EXH=1 HMAX=4 TMIN=8 TMAX=24 STALL=40 KICK=3 OUT=run1_best.in OUT0=cost0_run1.in timeout 700 nice -n 19 ./tabu start_f5.in
next: No gain in 94 steps: walk stays at cost 8-12 and never returns below 2. Flag swaps are far too destructive (min +170 to +240 per move); sigma swaps from hot points give +4 at cost 2 (f5) but +206 at cost 4 (q901). Next: a secondary objective (demand term) or 2-move lookahead on the plateau; start_g61 and start_r302 were not run.

idea: Keep best_f5 base fixed; free sigma on the 88 demand-involved points (demand-graph vertices and preimages of demanded lines). Tried: pysat demand CSP with move bound K plus full cost check (K=4 demand-preserving moves cost 38); exhaustive enumeration of demand-preserving neighbours (K<=6: 1442 solutions, min cost 34); restricted C annealer over the free points (best 2)
next: Coset-aware exact model: walk-level CNF over free jump literals for failing (s,t,coset) triples on a small free set. Demand-preserving changes within 6 points cost >=34 and the demand system alone is satisfiable globally (cost 1450), so a cost-0 sigma, if any, is far from best_f5.

idea: Multi-start search over regulus-switch choices (hyperbolic line h of 4160, bijective or ovoid-type transversal assignment pi for p_j, transversal tau for y_j, fix-2 lines m_j), randomised local search, then annealing of the three best starts (80, 82, 82). Only the first start finished its 600 s anneal (best 4); the second reached 6; the third was stopped at 8.
command: timeout 700 nice -n 19 python3 search.py 300 2; then SEED=1 SECS=600 T0=3 T1=0.1 PF=0.1 PH=0.7 MU=0 OUT=b<r>.in OUT0=zero<r>.in timeout 700 nice -n 19 ./plusopt5 top/s2_r<r>.in for r=0,1,2 (anneal3.sh)
next: Lowest start was 68 (top/s1_r0.in, seed 1). Annealing from it or from b0.in is untested. The regulus family plateaus at 4-8 under annealing, so try a different switch family (not the transversal grid).
